prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M. Out of scope: grid, port. Offshore Substation (Morrowick; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; Switching Window Acknowledgment); Main Transformer (site-specific trip); export cable→Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher if capability<target; applies Dispatcher ceiling); Grid Dispatcher: requirements→Relay. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; validated commands; Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode on aux loss; shutdown on confirmed fire), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet (isolated on fire/overheat), Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; Leading Edge Tile Image). Substation: Export Cable Monitor (alarms→Control Engineer), Fire Detection Panel, Emergency Generator (Foxglove; auto start on aux loss; no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace→Substation Operator), Helideck. Modes: Substation Degraded, Grid Constraint, Weather Hold, Vessel Standby, Turbine Lockout (no remote restart during fire investigation). Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard). Alarms: safety>protection>export; not cleared on detector reset. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; data→Shore Control Room; Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway). Shore Control Room (Amber Quay; hub; holds last limit on grid comms loss). Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale). Operations Radio Console (voice to CTV, SOV, Daughter Craft). Personnel Tracking Console (route entry/exit records). Weather Analyst: Wave Burst Record; Visibility Confidence Note→Duty Planner. Marine Coordinator: Berth Slot Confirmation. Vessel Master: Transfer Manifest Addendum; Crew Count Correction→Personnel Tracking Console. Recovery Basket Load Sheet→Rescue Coordinator. HSE Officer: evacuation advice. Field Supervisor: work status→Shore Control Room. North Access Scanner: credential/period/area check; deny otherwise; gate secured if unverifiable; no verbal override; unique transaction ID. Southern route scanner: credential/area/time authorization; timestamped logs; barrier closed on failure; anti-tailgating; escorts verified; faults→out of service; credential-free emergency egress. East Service Lift: interlock/overload checks; Electrical Technician checks supply faults; Field Supervisor records inspection. West Service Lift: operator checks doors, leveling, lighting, controls, emergency stop; interlocks functional, never

New part:
S912: Safety performance measures include reported events, completion of required controls, and timely closure of corrective actions.
S913: Performance definitions identify the source data, calculation method, reporting interval, and accountable owner for each measure.
S914: The SCADA Gateway provides operational records used to assess turbine availability and production trends.
S915: The Nacelle Condition Monitor supports assessment of equipment condition and emerging degradation.
S916: The Offshore Substation is reviewed for operational availability and the frequency and duration of equipment interruptions.
S917: The Fleet Dispatch Console provides a fleet-level view of operating status and response to emerging constraints.
S918: The Maintenance Planning Engine supports review of planned work, resource demand, and maintenance completion performance.
S919: Performance results are reviewed at regular operational meetings and escalated when approved thresholds are exceeded.
S920: The Control Engineer examines significant operational deviations and records the technical findings for review.
S921: Reliability reviews consider failure frequency, failure duration, recurrence, and the operational consequences of each event.
S922: Review teams distinguish equipment faults from external causes such as access limitations, weather conditions, and grid restrictions.
S923: Failure analyses use available operating history, inspection findings, and maintenance records to identify credible causes.
S924: Corrective actions are assigned an owner, due date, and verification method before they are tracked to closure.
S925: The Duty Planner uses reliability findings to adjust work priorities and planned maintenance intervals when justified.
S926: Lessons learned from maintenance campaigns and significant events are captured in a form that can be applied across the fleet.
S927: The Field Supervisor provides feedback on whether revised procedures and controls are practical during offshore work.
S928: The Warehouse System uses recurring failure and repair information to inform review of critical spares and replenishment assumptions.
S929: The Cybersecurity Analyst reviews performance records for evidence that cybersecurity controls affect operational availability or recovery.
S930: Changes to performance definitions or reporting logic are controlled so that trends remain comparable over time.
S931: Proposed reliability improvements are assessed for safety, technical feasibility, resource needs, and expected operational benefit.
S932: Approved improvements are monitored after implementation to confirm that they deliver the intended result and do not introduce adverse effects.
S933: The operational concept is reviewed periodically so that performance measures and lessons learned continue to reflect actual operating experience.
S934: A degraded mode is entered when a fault, communication loss, environmental limit, or external restriction prevents normal service without requiring immediate full-site shutdown.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
